metadata.description: A physical machine as a managed asset — the box itself, one of the three forms of Machine (CLS-004, by form). It may sit unallocated in inventory, carries its aggregate capacity (cpu, memory, storage) as host attributes, and is what VMs, containers and storage daemons ultimately run on. Allocating a host to a consumer is the ownership model, not a separate type; its components (NICs, drives, GPUs, BMC) are their own records contained by it. Grounded in Redfish ComputerSystem for inventory and Metal3 BareMetalHost for provisioning.

instance_size.description: Provider-neutral size class (small | medium | large, ordered and comparable; common-elements §2.2). Sizes the machine in place of explicit cpu and memory; the provider maps the class to concrete resources at realization. A machine may be declared by size class alone.

storage_tier.description: The requested storage performance class — a governed `storage_tier` term (standard | performance | archive), each denoting a requirements floor. Name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036): a tier name resolves to its floor, explicit `storage` requirements win where both are given, and any provider class that clears the floor qualifies. The provider records the native class it chose as a realized output. Profile decides whether a bare term or a data_reference is required. Governed vocabulary `storage_tier` (ADR-038 §2); name-selectable but requirements-authoritative (ADR-036). Profile decides bare-vs-reference.

disks.description: The machine's disks as portable intent, in order; each entry's `name` is the join key a realized Volume binds to through its `disk_entry`.

boot_order.description: Ordered boot devices: a `disks[].name`, or the device class `network` or `cdrom`.

mounts.description: Network file shares the guest mounts: a FileShare, one of its exports, a mount path, read-only.

source_ref.description: Reference to the FileShare serving the export.

share.description: The export to mount, a `shares[].name` on that FileShare.

mount_path.description: Absolute path in the guest where the share is mounted.

read_only.description: Mount read-only even where the export allows writes.

buckets.description: Buckets the machine's workloads use: a Bucket, the credential to reach it, read-only.

credential_ref.description: Reference to the CredentialRef the machine reaches the bucket with; never the secret itself.

guest_os.description: The requested operating system. Portable form: a data_reference to an `os_image` term the provider advertises. Inline `{type, version}` is the portability-breaking escape. Optional: a machine may be declared by sizing alone; a profile may require it.

type.description: Inline OS identifier (e.g. linux-server-9). portability_breaking: a value with no os_image vocabulary entry — a review finding.

run_state.description: The run state the consumer wants the provider to drive the machine to (`running`, `stopped`, `suspended`); the provider translates it to its native spec. Observed counterpart: `outputs.observed_run_state`.

composition_visibility.description: Whether the host's components are modeled as their own records or only as rollups on the host (`opaque`). CPU, memory and local storage stay rollups either way.

identity.description: Chassis and system identity: serial, model, asset tag.

image.description: The provisioning image written to the root device at provision time (Metal3 image). A host rebuilt from intent re-provisions from exactly this.

url.description: Image URL (artifact location, not a resource reference).

root_device_hints.description: Which disk receives the image (Metal3 rootDeviceHints), matched at provision time.

serial_number.description: Disk serial hint — the stable choice across reboots.

boot_interface_ref.description: Reference to the NetworkInterface the host network-boots from.

firmware.description: Host firmware: `type` is `legacy` or `uefi` (the Redfish spelling Machine.VM shares) plus UEFI Secure Boot. No vTPM here: a physical TPM is a hardware fact. Not on Machine because an LPAR cannot honour it.

type.description: Firmware interface the host boots with (Redfish spelling; `legacy` is BIOS).

secure_boot.description: UEFI Secure Boot. Only valid with type: uefi (policy-validated).

realized_volumes.description: DERIVED: per-disk realization map, items {entry, volume, storage_backing}. For each `disks[].name`, the Volume realizing it (by the volume's `realizes_disk` edge and `disk_entry` join key) and the native storage class the provider chose, the ADR-036 realized fact behind the entry's `storage_tier`. Computed from the Volume records, never stored (compute-never-store); the lineage surface from declared disk to realized volume.

observed_run_state.description: The run state the provider last observed, normalized to the same vocabulary as `run_state` (Redfish PowerState On and Off, a KubeVirt phase, an HMC partition state all land here; PoweringOn and PoweringOff are `transitioning`). Drives shutdown and startup ordering for the dependency graph. One output for every form of Machine (row 111).

provider_handle.description: The provider-native identifier of the realized machine (opaque; correlation and operations only — never a portable reference). Promoted from Machine.VM: every form has one.

primary_ip.description: The primary or management address of the booted machine — the single address most bindings want. Promoted from Machine.VM: a bare-metal host and an LPAR have one once booted.

hostname.description: Realized hostname (FQDN where the realm provides one). Promoted from Machine.VM.

management_address.description: Reachable management endpoint (BMC/Redfish or host management IP) once Realized. When a BMC record exists for this host, the BMC record is authoritative; this output is the convenience copy.

os_image_digest.description: Content digest of the OS image the host actually runs — the Realized twin of spec.image.checksum. Answers 'which hosts run which image, and which have never converged?' from declared outputs: season-pin != os_image_digest is the derivable never-converged / stale-image fact, without restating the image record.

effective_config_digest.description: Digest of the resolved effective configuration this host last converged to — the Realized twin of the assembled request. The comparable fact only: per-field values and their winning layers are reconstructable from the layer chain + provenance (LAY-008), never restated here. Pairs with os_image_digest to make requested-vs-realized configuration a first-class, bindable comparison per host.

relationships.name: mounts
relationships.description: Declared on the machine: its guest mounts an export of this FileShare (spec.mounts names which). The consumer declares the edge, so a share never lists the machines that mount it.

relationships.name: buckets
relationships.description: Declared on the machine: its workloads use this bucket (spec.buckets names it).

relationships.name: bucket_credential
relationships.description: The credential a `buckets` entry reaches its bucket with (spec.buckets[].credential_ref).
Power source(s) the host draws from; the host stops before the feed in a reverse-topo shutdown.

adopts.role: Vendor-neutral compute-system representation spanning physical, virtual and partitioned (Redfish ComputerSystem SystemType: Physical | Virtual | Composed | PhysicallyPartitioned | VirtuallyPartitioned) — the one representative standard for the Machine family, shared by Machine.VM, Machine.BareMetalHost and Machine.LPAR and declared once here. Nova with Ironic, Cluster API's Machine and TOSCA's Compute are the industry abstractions that treat the three forms as one thing (CLS-002 (a)); Redfish is the wire representation adopted. Provider-native realizations are declared on the provider support matrix, not on the substrate type.
the `buckets` claim (a BucketClaim's role) and its credential (a BucketAccess, held as a CredentialRef)
mount field names for `mounts` (mountPath, readOnly), snake_case, shared with UDLM's Container `mounts`

bare-metal provisioning lifecycle + available/provisioned state; the provider translates `run_state.desired_state` into `online` (running = true, stopped = false) and reads bootMACAddress from the referenced boot interface

context.purpose: Models a physical machine as a managed asset — the box itself, whether or not anything is running on it yet.
context.plain_description: One physical server: its identity (serial, model, asset tag), its aggregate capacity (CPU sockets and cores, memory, local storage), and its lifecycle state. It can sit unallocated in inventory before anything is deployed on it. Components like NICs can be modeled as their own records attached to the host; CPU, memory, and disk normally stay as rollup numbers on the host itself. Everything that runs — VMs, containers, storage daemons — ultimately sits on one of these, which makes it a central node in shutdown and startup ordering.
use_when: You need an inventory of physical servers, including ones not yet assigned to any workload.
You need the dependency chain workload → host → power feed, so an outage or maintenance walk knows what stops when.
You need per-host aggregate capacity (cores, memory, storage) for allocation decisions.
you need host provisioning to be replayable intent — image, root device, boot MAC, power target — so a lost host rebuilds from the estate (the bare-metal leg of rehydration)
not_for: A virtual machine — that is Machine.VM; a host is hardware you can touch.
The host's out-of-band management controller — that is BMC, its own record with its own address and power-control surface.
Individual NICs, GPUs, or drives inside the host — those are NetworkInterface / GPU / StorageDevice records contained by the host.
works_with: PowerFeed — the power source the host draws from; roots the shutdown ordering.
The host's own `firmware` element — the portable BIOS settings it converges to; vendor attribute sets are Provider Class data.
NetworkInterface, StorageDevice, GPU, BMC — the host's components, as contained records.
Machine.VM — the guests the host runs.
